narrative:
The model estimated a 52% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, which is just above the bank’s denial threshold, so your loan application was not approved. The decision was not based on your age, sex or foreign-worker status, but on patterns in your application.

The strongest influence was your savings. Having at least 1,000 DM in savings is uncommon among approved applicants—only about 3% have this—so this worked strongly in your favour and pushed toward good credit. The second most important factor was the loan purpose: a new car pushed toward bad credit, as new-car lending is less common among approved applicants than loans for radio/TV or furniture. Third was your checking-account status: a balance between 0 and 200 DM pushed toward bad credit, since most approved applicants either have no checking account or a different balance profile.

Overall, the favourable savings signal was outweighed by these risk signals, leaving your estimated risk just over the line. Next, ask the bank what specifically would make a future application stronger. You could discuss reducing the installment rate from 4% of disposable income, which is above the approved average of about 3%, adding a co-applicant or guarantor, and building a more stable checking-account balance before reapplying.
